neighbours.label: ' off' in the getaway phrasal verb 'make/made off (with)': the particle that stands between the verb and an expected 'with'
fire: During the night, burglars made off with the shop's entire stock of watches.
A fox got into the coop and made off with two of the hens.
While we were swimming, a monkey made off with my sunglasses.
The con man gained her trust and then made off with her savings.
Raiders broke the window and made off with a tray of rings.
Before anyone noticed, the seagull had made off with his sandwich.
The gang tied up the guard and made off with the payroll.
Somebody cut the lock and made off with three bicycles.
quiet: During the night, burglars stole the shop's entire stock of watches.
A fox got into the coop and killed two of the hens.
While we were swimming, a monkey took off across the rocks.
The con man gained her trust and then paid off his own debts.
Raiders broke the window and grabbed a tray of rings.
Before anyone noticed, the seagull had set off towards the pier.
The gang tied up the guard and switched off the alarm.
Somebody cut the lock and stole three bicycles.

notes: Card top examples share no token (they, ',', be, off, and); the + pole fires on 'start/ends/separated' before 'with' and promotes ' with'. Probe: 'thieves made off with' 0.55 on ' off'; the other card-like frames 0.00-0.11. Near misses use other 'off' phrasal verbs or theft without the phrase.
